_comment: Authoring contract handed to every Phase B (per-RGD authoring) subagent. Static JSON so N concurrent authors converge on the same conventions. Update in ONE place; never fork per subagent.

labels._purpose: Selection-friendly, regex-constrained ([A-Za-z0-9._-]). Applied on RGD and on every rendered CR under resources/.

required.rekoncile.io/rgd: RGD name owning this resource, e.g. rekoncile-demo-app-stack-adopt

on_rgd_only.rekoncile.io/source-path: slash-sanitized path — replace every '/' with '-', e.g. module-5-rds-tf-baseline
on_rgd_only.rekoncile.io/tf-module: TF module the RGD represents, e.g. vpc, eks, root

annotations._purpose: Free-form, no regex constraints. Carry exact TF traceability info that would fail label validation.

required_on_rendered_cr.rekoncile.io/from-tf-address: Exact TF address including brackets, e.g. module.vpc.aws_subnet.public[0]
required_on_rendered_cr.rekoncile.io/tf-attributes: JSON map {ackField: 'tf.attribute.source or explanation'} for every populated field

services.k8s.aws/adoption-policy.when_to_use_adopt: Strict import — ACK reads spec from live state. Ideal spec: {}.
services.k8s.aws/adoption-policy.when_to_use_adopt_or_create: You want the CR to double as create-if-missing. Fully populated spec required.

adoption_annotations.services.k8s.aws/adoption-fields: Lookup JSON per resource type. Keys per adoption_fields_by_kind below.

services.k8s.aws/deletion-policy.rationale: Prevents accidental deletion of live AWS resource if CR is removed.

spec_shape.reality: Most ACK v1.x CRDs enforce OpenAPI required-field validation even on adopt. Populate ONLY the required subset with live values. Add comment '# CRD-required minimum on adopt; ACK re-reads on adopt.'

create_mode_rules.spec_shape: Fully populated. Cross-refs inside an RGD use KRO refs (roleRef.from.name / vpcRef.from.name / targetKeyRef.from.name) not string interpolation, unless referring to status.ackResourceMetadata.arn.
create_mode_rules.parameterization: Every value that comes from a Terraform variable becomes a schema.spec field with the TF default preserved.

namespace.rule: REQUIRED in every resource template metadata block
namespace.derivation: Use the target namespace passed as Namespace input parameter. Never omit — KRO will place the CR in the controller default namespace if missing, breaking ServiceAccount references.
namespace.example:
metadata:
  name: ...
  namespace: webapp-rds  # always explicit

template_top_level_keys.rule: A resource template's top-level keys MUST be exactly apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec (plus data/stringData/type for native ConfigMap/Secret, rules for RBAC). annotations and labels MUST be nested under metadata, never peers of it.
template_top_level_keys.why: resources[].template is x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true, so the API server accepts a mis-indented key and kubectl apply --dry-run=server passes. The failure surfaces only at RGD reconciliation as 'error getting field schema for path .<key>: schema not found for field <key>', with the RGD wedged GraphAccepted=False.
template_top_level_keys.incorrect:
template:
  metadata:
    name: x
  annotations:        # <-- peer of metadata; kro rejects the RGD
template_top_level_keys.automated_gate: scripts/run validate-spec-fields <rgd.yaml> — flags any top-level template key outside the allowed set for that Kind, regardless of its value type. A mis-indented annotations/labels block is flagged even though its value is an object.

immutable_spec_fields.rule: Use literal values, NEVER CEL expressions, for fields marked x-kubernetes-validations: self == oldSelf. Using CEL causes permanent FAILED state if the instance spec is ever updated.
immutable_spec_fields.enforcement: Do not trust the list below — it is a non-exhaustive snapshot. Before writing any spec field that looks like a name or identifier, enumerate the immutable fields from the live CRD: kubectl get crd <plural>.<group> -o json | python3 -c "import sys,json; c=json.load(sys.stdin); p=c['spec']['versions'][0]['schema']['openAPIV3Schema']['properties']['spec']['properties']; [print(k) for k in p if p[k].get('x-kubernetes-validations')]"
immutable_spec_fields._known_immutable_fields_note: Snapshot only, verified 2026-09 against controller main. The RDS DBInstance CRD marks several more fields immutable; always run the enforcement command instead of relying on this list.

pre_write_crd_field_check.rule: Before writing any spec field in a CR template, verify the field exists in the LIVE CRD. If it is absent, do NOT include it — record the omission in MIGRATION-NOTES.md under 'Unsupported TF attributes'.
pre_write_crd_field_check.rationale: AWS SDK/API parameters and Terraform lifecycle arguments are not the same set as ACK CRD spec fields. Reading the AWS service docs is NOT sufficient evidence that a field exists in the CRD.
pre_write_crd_field_check.where_each_gate_bites: STANDALONE CR under resources/: kubectl apply --dry-run=server DOES reject an unknown spec field. kubectl's default is --validate=true, i.e. strict server-side field validation, and Strict returns 400 naming every unknown field; field validation is stable since Kubernetes 1.27 and its feature gate has been removed. Unknown fields are pruned without signal only at the Ignore/Warn levels. RGD TEMPLATE: dry-run cannot see inside it, because resources[].template is x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true — the one documented exception to pruning and to strict validation. The failure surfaces at RGD reconciliation as 'error getting field schema for path spec.<field>: schema not found for field <field>'. CONSEQUENCE: validate-spec-fields is the ONLY gate for the rgd.yaml half and a cheap second opinion on the resources/ half. Do not justify it with a pruning claim that is false for CRs. Ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/api-concepts/
pre_write_crd_field_check.command: kubectl get crd <plural>.<group> -o jsonpath='{.spec.versions[0].schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec.properties}' | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(sorted(d.keys()))"
pre_write_crd_field_check.command_note: versions[0] is correct for ACK CRDs, which currently ship a single v1alpha1 version. If a CRD ever serves multiple versions, select the one with storage: true instead.
pre_write_crd_field_check.automated_gate: scripts/run validate-spec-fields <resources-dir> — checks every spec key in generated CRs against the live CRD and exits non-zero on unknown fields.
pre_write_crd_field_check.asserting_absence_parse_dont_grep: When asserting a field is absent from a generated artifact, parse the YAML and check KEYS — never grep raw text. A correct file may legitimately mention an omitted field in a comment explaining the omission, so a text match proves nothing. Observed: all 7 checked fields (recoveryWindowInDays, secretString, skipFinalSnapshot, applyImmediately, availabilityZone among them) initially flagged as PRESENT by a raw-text grep and needed a second pass to confirm they were comment-only. With the comment_budget rule these mentions get rarer but do not disappear — a one-line 'omitted: absent from this CRD' note is exactly the kind of non-obvious constraint the budget still permits.

known_absent_fields._note: Non-authoritative snapshot (verified 2026-09 against each controller's main branch). The live enumeration above always wins. Controllers add fields over time — never omit a field solely because it appears here without re-checking.

secretsmanager.services.k8s.aws/Secret.note: forceDeleteWithoutRecovery is not a CRD spec field. recoveryWindowInDays is VERSION-DEPENDENT: added upstream in secretsmanager-controller v1.6.0 (absent at the v1.5.0 tag, present at v1.6.0 — verified by tag diff) and absent on every earlier controller. ENUMERATE THE LIVE CRD before writing it (verified absent on an EKS Auto Mode managed capability cluster in 2026-09). If present, map TF recovery_window_in_days (0 requests immediate deletion via the DeleteSecret ForceDeleteWithoutRecovery parameter). If absent, OMIT it and record it under 'Unsupported TF attributes' — in a CR the strict dry-run rejects it, and in an RGD template it wedges the RGD at reconciliation. Never write this field on the basis of this note alone.

rds.services.k8s.aws/DBInstance.note: skipFinalSnapshot and finalSnapshotIdentifier are Terraform deletion-lifecycle arguments with no ACK CRD field. applyImmediately is an AWS API request parameter not exposed in the CRD spec. Omit all three and record them as unsupported TF attributes.

readyWhen_scope.rule: A resource's readyWhen MUST reference ONLY that same resource, by its own id. It MUST NOT reference another resource id or schema. kro validates this at RGD creation and rejects cross-resource readyWhen with 'references unknown identifiers: [<other-id>]'.
readyWhen_scope.ordering: Cross-resource ordering is NEVER expressed in readyWhen. kro infers the dependency graph from CEL references in TEMPLATE fields: when resource A's template interpolates ${b.status...}, kro creates B, waits for B's own readyWhen, then creates A.
readyWhen_scope.no_natural_reference: If a resource's template has no natural sibling reference (e.g. an adopted DBInstance or PodIdentityAssociation whose spec is all tfstate literals) but must still be ordered after a sibling, add a traceability annotation on that resource's template that interpolates the sibling status, e.g. metadata.annotations['rekoncile.io/depends-on-role']: ${role.status.ackResourceMetadata.arn}. Never move the dependency into readyWhen.

adoption_fields_templating.rule: CEL interpolation inside services.k8s.aws/adoption-fields IS SUPPORTED and is the intended pattern for an adopt-mode RGD. Example: services.k8s.aws/adoption-fields: '{"vpcID":"${schema.spec.vpcID}"}'
adoption_fields_templating.why: Parameterizing the lookup on schema.spec is what makes one adopt RGD reusable across accounts and regions — only instance.yaml changes. Do NOT 'fix' a templated adoption-fields value by replacing it with a literal.
adoption_fields_templating.constraint: Reference only ${schema.spec.*} / ${schema.metadata.*} in adoption-fields. Do not reference a sibling resource's status: the lookup must resolve before the resource is created, so a status reference cannot be satisfied.
adoption_fields_templating.note: The result after CEL evaluation must still be valid JSON. Keep the surrounding quoting intact.
adoption_fields_templating.misdiagnosis_warning: An RGD error naming .annotations ('schema not found for field annotations') is NOT caused by CEL in adoption-fields. It means the annotations block is mis-indented as a peer of metadata — see template_top_level_keys.

spec_field_values.rule: ALL spec field values MUST be extracted from terraform.tfstate attributes. Never invent plausible-sounding values (descriptions, names, ARNs). If the TF state attribute is empty, use the literal string 'Managed by Terraform' for description fields.
spec_field_values.rationale: ACK reconciles spec against live state. An invented value causes drift detection → ACK attempts to mutate the live AWS resource to match.

comment_budget.rule: Comments MUST NOT exceed ~10% of a generated file's bytes.
comment_budget.allowed: A <=3-line header naming the targeted KRO/ACK version, and ONE short line where a value's provenance or a constraint is genuinely non-obvious (an immutable field kept literal; a field deliberately omitted because it is absent from the live CRD; a consolidated child's TF origin).
comment_budget.not_allowed: ASCII separator/banner blocks; multi-line per-resource preambles; restating the phase narrative, the adoption-policy semantics, or anything already in report.html / MIGRATION-NOTES.md. Provenance belongs in the rekoncile.io/{from-tf-address,tf-attributes} annotations — which are load-bearing and machine-readable — not in prose beside them.
comment_budget.rationale: Generated YAML is emitted serially on one agent's critical path, so comment bytes are wall-clock. Measured: rgd.yaml at 35% comments (6,008 of 17,223 B) inside an 82-second single write, with the same content already rendered in two other artifacts — that one file was 1.9x the size of all seven rendered CRs combined. The skill already forbids duplicating the decision record between MIGRATION-NOTES.md and decisions.json; this extends the same rule to the YAML, where the narrative was reappearing a third time.

omission_is_not_destructive.rule: KRO applies every rendered template via server-side apply ONLY. A field the template omits is NOT stripped — KRO can only remove fields it previously owned. Do NOT claim an ACK sync-and-delete path is triggered by template omission without naming what actually sets the field to empty.
omission_is_not_destructive.verified_kro: kro @ 0e8582fd9307bcdba6fe5d6b34becd3f41f4590a (main, 2026-09-24). Every write to a rendered template is server-side apply: ssaApply (pkg/graphengine/executor/simple.go:1603, `Patch(ctx, obj, client.Apply, opts...)`) called from applyTemplateObject (simple.go:2166) with FieldManager 'kro.run/applyset' and force=true. The desired object is a DeepCopy of the template with CEL results written only at compiler-recorded paths — never merged with the live object, never round-tripped through a typed struct, never schema-defaulted. Two render-path passes (cleanOmitSentinels, cleanPendingValues) DELETE placeholder keys rather than nulling them, so an omitted field is absent from the apply body and never enters kro's managedFields entry. Templates are re-applied unchanged on resync (default ~10h) with a byte-identical body, so ownership never transitions owned->absent, which is the only thing that triggers SSA deletion. Zero .Update() calls on rendered child resources in pkg/controller/instance/ or pkg/graphengine/ outside tests.
omission_is_not_destructive.verified_ack: aws-controllers-k8s/runtime @ 26e42fd9135662cec2d54cef2df74b55c6bafc4f (main, 2026-09-16). THE MECHANISM IS THE SPEC BACKFILL, NOT AN UNREACHABLE CODE PATH — do not restate it as 'the runtime never calls updateResource', which is false. The adoption gate is one line at reconciler.go:592 (`NeedAdoption(desired) && !r.rd.IsManaged(desired) && FeatureGates.IsEnabled(ResourceAdoption)`); the adopt arm is 673-685; 595-601 is only the `if !needAdoption { adoptionPolicy = "" }` normalization and contains no call to patchResourceMetadataAndSpec. Sync is an if/else-if chain, so reconcile #1 structurally skips updateResource, but the adopt arm does NOT return — and on reconcile #2 the persisted adopted annotation makes NeedAdoption() false, the policy is blanked, and execution DOES reach updateResource. What makes that safe: patchResourceMetadataAndSpec (adopt arm) patches the SPEC OF THE STORED KUBERNETES OBJECT with the ReadOne-observed values, so on reconcile #2+ both delta sides derive from the same ReadOne projection, the spec delta is empty, and rm.Update is never invoked. Safety rests on a SUCCESSFUL BACKFILL PATCH — see backfill_failure_race. Cite by symbol name, not line number: these numbers rot, and line-number rot is exactly how this claim previously came to be stated via a mechanism its own citation did not support.
omission_is_not_destructive.consequence: Because the adopt-path backfill makes the ACK controller the field owner of live-populated spec fields (tags, ingressRules/egressRules, policies), a KRO template that omits them is a genuine no-op. Populating them anyway is prudent, self-documenting, prevents Terraform drift during co-management, AND mitigates the backfill_failure_race below — but under adoption-policy: adopt it is NOT preventing a strip.
omission_is_not_destructive.how_to_reason: A destructive-on-omit claim needs BOTH halves: (1) the controller's sync path deletes live-minus-desired, AND (2) something persistently presents the field as empty desired state. Half (1) is common across ACK controllers and is NOT worth researching — do not spawn an agent for it (see SKILL.md § Parallel Phase A, 'Do NOT audit destructive-reconcile-on-omit'). Half (2) is the deciding half: NOT satisfied by adoption-policy: adopt (spec backfill, above) nor by KRO (SSA, above); IS satisfied by adopt-or-create and by the backfill-failure race below. Verify half (2) before warning the operator; overstating it has previously driven both a wrong Decision_Summary and an unnecessary multi-minute research agent.
omission_is_not_destructive.backfill_failure_race: REAL FAILURE MODE, and the reason the guidance to enumerate children is more than cosmetic. setResourceManagedAndAdopted issues its OWN patch persisting the finalizer + adopted annotation, and only AFTERWARDS does the adopt arm patch the spec backfill. The metadata+spec patch has NO conflict retry (unlike patchStatus, which uses retry.RetryOnConflict). If the backfill patch fails — transient API error, 409 from a concurrent writer, webhook rejection — the CR is left adopted+managed in etcd with the user's sparse spec. On the next reconcile NeedAdoption is false, the policy is blanked, updateResource runs, the spec delta IS different, and ACK pushes empty/nil values for every omitted field. Narrow race, not the common case, but it is the concrete reason to enumerate tags and consolidated children in adopt CRs rather than relying on the backfill.
omission_is_not_destructive.adopt_or_create_exception: SCOPE LIMIT: everything above applies to adoption-policy: adopt. It does NOT apply to adopt-or-create, which NEVER backfills the spec. Under that policy only the STATUS is taken from the populated object ('here we assume the spec fields are provided in the spec'), and when ReadOne succeeds the arm marks the resource managed+adopted and requeues WITHOUT calling patchResourceMetadataAndSpec. On the requeue the policy is blanked and updateResource runs against the user's declared spec — satisfying half (2), so a rule-less or tag-less spec DOES drive syncSGRules -> Revoke* and DeleteTags. Use adoption-policy: adopt for brownfield adoption; if adopt-or-create is ever justified, the spec MUST fully enumerate live rules and tags. Related: adding adoption-policy: adopt to an ALREADY-managed CR never triggers adoption at all (the gate requires !IsManaged), so no backfill happens and the normal update path runs on the first reconcile.
omission_is_not_destructive.kro_force_inverse_risk: THE INVERSE RISK, equally important: because the instance path applies with force=true and ConflictDetection=false, any field the template DOES mention is force-stolen from the ACK controller's field manager and reasserted on every reconcile including the ~10h resync, with NO conflict surfaced. force=true does not extend ownership to unmentioned fields (it only resolves conflicts for fields in the apply body), but for fields both ACK and KRO write, expect silent flip-flop rather than an error. Consequence for adopt RGDs: enumerate live values accurately, because whatever you put in the template WILL win repeatedly.
omission_is_not_destructive.kro_pruning_is_whole_object: SCOPE OF 'no pruning': field-level nullify/prune genuinely does not exist, but do NOT generalize that to 'no pruning exists in kro'. KEP-3659 ApplySet pruning is a real, prominent subsystem (pkg/controller/instance/applyset/). It operates at WHOLE-OBJECT granularity: orphaned applyset members whose UID is absent from KeepUIDs are DELETED (UID-guarded via Preconditions), gated on the graph being fully resolved. It never rewrites fields on a surviving object. So: omitting a FIELD is safe; dropping a whole RESOURCE from an RGD DELETES the live object.
omission_is_not_destructive.readone_gaps_are_silent: A spec field the service's ReadOne does not populate stays nil in the backfilled spec, so the adopted CR silently misrepresents live AWS state for that field. Non-destructive (both delta sides are nil) but it means an adopted CR is not a reliable record of live configuration.
omission_is_not_destructive.feature_gate: ResourceAdoption is Beta with Enabled: true in the runtime's defaultACKFeatureGates — ON BY DEFAULT. Do NOT flag it to the operator as an unverifiable risk; that is overcautious. It can still be explicitly disabled, in which case adoption annotations are ignored and the CR is treated as a CREATE.

naming_conventions._rationale: All names derived algorithmically from the ACK Kind — no static per-TF-type table needed. Guarantees workshop doc commands match generated output regardless of stack.

cr_metadata_name.rule: Kind to kebab-case: split on PascalCase word boundaries, lowercase, join with hyphens

rgd_resource_id.note: This value becomes kro.run/node-id label on the managed CR — workshop validation commands depend on it.

rgd_schema_status_field.note: Used in workshop jsonpath commands: kubectl get <Kind> -o jsonpath='{.status.roleARN}'

canonical_schema_spec_field_names._rationale: Fixed field names prevent KRO breaking-change errors on re-generation (rename = field removal = CRD update rejected).
canonical_schema_spec_field_names.aws_secretsmanager_secret.name: smSecretName
canonical_schema_spec_field_names.aws_db_subnet_group.name: dbSubnetGroupName
canonical_schema_spec_field_names.aws_iam_role.name: iamRoleName

adoption_fields_by_kind.iam.services.k8s.aws/Policy: {"arn": "arn:aws:iam::<acct>:policy/<name>"}  // arn ONLY — name can NEVER resolve: IAM GetPolicy has no name-based lookup, so the CR sits in NotFound forever. Read the ARN from tfstate attributes.arn.

consolidation_rules._purpose: TF resources that ACK folds into a parent CR. Do NOT emit as separate CRs.
consolidation_rules.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment: NEVER skip silently. Extract `policy_arn` from the attachment resource and populate `spec.policies: [<policy_arn>]` on the parent Role CR. The iam-controller's syncManagedPolicies detach path is real: Role.spec.policies is fully declarative, and a managed policy attached in AWS but absent from the array is detached. Adoption does not trigger it — under adoption-policy: adopt the runtime backfills the ReadOne-observed spec into the CR, so later reconciles compare ReadOne against ReadOne and the spec delta is empty; see rgd_template_rules.omission_is_not_destructive.verified_ack, and note backfill_failure_race and adopt_or_create_exception there. So populate it because it is prudent, self-documenting, prevents Terraform drift during co-management, and mitigates that race — NOT because an immediate detach is pending. Do NOT describe omission as causing immediate permission loss under adoption-policy: adopt.
consolidation_rules.aws_route_table_association: Merged into ec2/RouteTable.spec.associations (or reference the RouteTable from Subnet, controller-dependent).
consolidation_rules.aws_security_group_rule: Merged into ec2/SecurityGroup.spec.{ingressRules,egressRules}. There is NO standalone rule Kind in ec2-controller — verified against main: 20 CRDs in config/crd/bases, none is SecurityGroupRule, and there is no pkg/resource/security_group_rule package. A SecurityGroupRule Go type does exist but is status-only, surfaced read-only as SecurityGroup.status.rules[]; do not mistake it for an adoptable Kind. Still verify per-controller for other services. Enumerate BOTH rule directions from tfstate: the ec2-controller's syncSGRules revoke path is real, but under adoption-policy: adopt the spec backfill means omission does not sever live rules — see rgd_template_rules.omission_is_not_destructive, including backfill_failure_race and adopt_or_create_exception. Enumerate because it is prudent and keeps the first reconcile delta-free, NOT to avert an immediate revoke.
consolidation_rules.aws_ec2_tag: Merged into target resource's spec.tags list.
consolidation_rules.aws_route: Merged into ec2/RouteTable.spec.routes[]. Note: apigatewayv2/Route is unrelated to VPC routes.

grounding_loop._purpose: Every Phase B subagent runs this loop before returning success.
steps: 4. If any severity=error: re-author the offending resource, go to step 2.
5. Return success only after both validators return 0 errors OR 3 attempts have been made.
grounding_loop.escalation: If attempts_needed >= 3 with unresolved errors, main skill surfaces to operator at Phase 4 checkpoint.
grounding_loop.gate_commands_are_pre_supplied: Your fan-out prompt contains the exact, copy-paste-ready command line for every gate you must run. Do NOT read scripts/*.py source to work out invocation syntax — if a command is missing from your prompt, that is a defect in the prompt, not a research task for you. Reading a helper script is warranted ONLY when you are authoring a JSON input file that the script consumes (e.g. decisions.json for render_report.py), never to run a validator.
grounding_loop.passed_gate_is_final: When a gate returns zero severity=error findings, you are DONE. Do not re-read or re-inspect the file to 'confirm' — the validator's exit code IS the confirmation. Re-running a passed gate is duplicated work on the critical path.

capability_role_trust_policy.note: EKS capability roles use a DIFFERENT trust relationship from cluster (eks.amazonaws.com) and node (ec2.amazonaws.com) roles. Every dedicated capability role must use this trust policy.
